📌 Lock-and-Mint Bridges: Why Tokens Don’t Literally “Move” Across Chains

Main Points
⏺️ When assets move between chains, they often don’t transfer directly
⏺️ The original token may be locked on one chain while a copy is minted on another
⏺️ This post explains why bridges are useful, but add trust to the storage mechanism

1️⃣ Core Idea — a bridge receives an asset on one chain and creates a representation of it on another.
2️⃣ How It Works — the token can be locked in a contract, while a wrapped version is minted on the destination chain.
3️⃣ Risk Surface — if the bridge contract is hacked or governance is weak, the backed tokens can lose credibility.
4️⃣ What Matters — users should understand who controls the bridge, how transfers are verified, and where collateral is stored.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — before moving large amounts, check the bridge history, audits, limits, and supported networks.

Final Thoughts

Bridges make crypto easier to use, but they add a new risk layer. The asset may look the same, but its safety now depends on bridge infrastructure too.

Gaza Ministry of Health has now released mortality numbers for 2025. For the first time since the war, they give numbers for all deaths, including natural deaths. 

In 2025 there were a total of 24,650 deaths in Gaza. 18,870 (76.6%) of these were violent, of which 17,286 (70.1%) were due to "war operations" and 1,584 (6.4%) were classified as accidents. There were a total of 5,780 (23.4%) non-violent deaths, including disease, old age, and all other causes.

5,780 deaths is about the same as the annual non-violent mortality in Gaza before the war, and the age distribution is similar to 2022. There is no significant excess of non-violent deaths. 

In other words, despite frequent and loud claims to the contrary, there seems to be very few indirect deaths due to the war in Gaza in 2025.

As there were 50,227 births in 2025, this gives a natural population growth of 25,577 or 1.2% in Gaza in 2025, which is higher population growth than most countries in the world and more than the world average. 

There are currently ~6,000 births/month in Gaza, per GMH. Assuming a similar number of non-violent deaths in Gaza in 2026 as in 2025, that means there are currently 12x more births than deaths in Gaza, and that Gaza is now experiencing one of the highest population growths in the world.
